stories.title: Nvidia posts a record $115.8 billion quarter as its board rules out Jensen Huang's return
stories.deck: Interim chief executive Colette Kress says the roadmap is on track, while chair Harvey Jones says the board will not reinstate the founder.
summary: Nvidia reported the strongest quarter in its history on Tuesday, and then spent the first minutes of its earnings call making clear that its founder will not be coming back. Revenue for the third quarter of its 2027 fiscal year was about $115.8 billion, roughly double the figure a year earlier, and the first time quarterly sales have passed $100 billion. The Verge reports that data-centre revenue rose 110 per cent to $107.6 billion, that profit reached $65.3 billion, and that the company guided to about $130 billion in the fourth quarter. The Indian Express reported that the shares rose nearly 4 per cent in extended trading.

It was the first results call under interim chief executive Colette Kress, who took over after Jensen Huang resigned last week. She said the company's momentum "is real" and that its Vera Rubin product line is off to an "explosive start". Neither the results statement nor her prepared remarks addressed Huang's departure.

That task fell to Harvey Jones, Nvidia's first board chair. He told analysts the board had unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO", and that the company would not take questions about the circumstances or the ongoing investigation. His statement followed one Huang posted on X earlier in the day, in which he said he had not lived up to expected standards, regretted his mistakes and would be "honoured" to return if the board asked.

The background is a scandal that broke last week. Reports said Huang had affairs, including one with a former executive of the chip firm Megaspeed whom some outlets describe as an alleged Chinese asset, and one with a direct report. Nvidia says it is investigating whether the first relationship compromised national security or company secrets. Huang is due to testify to lawmakers on 1 December. None of the allegations about espionage has been proved in public.

stories.title: Nvidia says it will stop selling H200 chips in China, and a regulator is reportedly looking at the company
stories.deck: Kress tells investors the new stance will not dent revenue because of a backlog of demand elsewhere; TechCrunch notes Beijing already prefers domestic chips.
summary: Nvidia's interim chief executive has told investors the company is done selling its H200 AI chips to China, a sharp change of tone from the era when founder Jensen Huang argued that giving up the Chinese market would be a mistake. Speaking on the quarterly earnings call, Colette Kress said the decision would have no effect on top-line revenue because demand elsewhere is so strong that a backlog already exists, according to TechCrunch's account of the call.

Huang said in an April podcast that conceding China was a disservice to the industry. His resignation last week, after reports of affairs including one with a former Megaspeed executive described as an alleged Chinese asset, has put his China strategy under scrutiny. President Donald Trump has said national security was not put at risk and questioned whether the woman is really a spy; that claim is unproven, and China has denied it.

Analysts quoted by TechCrunch doubt that much was being lost anyway. Jacob Feldgoise said Beijing prefers to build demand for domestic chip infrastructure rather than accept Nvidia shipments. Separately, Dan Fisher-Owens said large data centres wanting to buy Nvidia chips must now certify that they do not serve Chinese customers, a sign of how tightly Washington has drawn its export rules.

There was one more headline from a busy day. The Wall Street Journal reported, as relayed by TechCrunch, that the US Securities and Exchange Commission is opening a probe into Nvidia following Huang's departure. Neither the regulator nor the company has publicly confirmed it, so it should be treated as a report, not a finding.

stories.title: Waymo pauses freeway rides in every market after California orders its highway service restricted
stories.deck: The state DMV calls driverless freeway operations an imminent safety hazard after repeated incursions into construction zones.
summary: Alphabet's robotaxi company Waymo has suspended freeway rides across all the markets where it operates after California's Department of Motor Vehicles restricted its highway operations. The regulator said Waymo's driverless freeway service poses an imminent hazard to public safety because its vehicles have repeatedly strayed into active construction zones, TechCrunch reports. The restrictions will stay in place until Waymo shows it has taken effective corrective action to fix the deficiencies.

Waymo spokesperson Dana Gallagher said safety is the foundation of everything the company does. She said that after recent encounters with freeway construction zones on US 101 the DMV imposed an operating restriction, and that Waymo had chosen to temporarily limit freeway operations in its other markets as well while it evaluates performance. She added that service on surface streets continues and covers more than half a million trips a week, and that the company is working to resume freeway rides.

The pause is a setback for a company that had made highway travel a selling point of its service, since freeways cut journey times for passengers heading to airports and between cities. Surface-street operations are not affected by the order.

The timing is awkward for a sector that is racing to expand. In the same TechCrunch report, Uber chief executive Dara Khosrowshahi is quoted saying Las Vegas will become the first US city where riders can use two fully driverless partners through the Uber app, starting with limited fleets and growing over the coming months.

stories.title: Amazon and Google would own almost 30 per cent of Anthropic after its IPO
stories.deck: Amazon's stake would be just under 15 per cent, with the option to go far higher; Google would hold nearly 14 per cent.
summary: Two of the world's biggest cloud companies would together control almost three tenths of Anthropic once the AI developer lists its shares, according to figures reported by TechCrunch. Amazon would hold 14.7 per cent after the initial public offering and Google 13.7 per cent, together close to 30 per cent. The report draws on details of how the two companies' earlier investments convert into equity.

Amazon's position is the more flexible of the two. TechCrunch says the company holds promissory notes that convert at either $2.09 or $5.05 per share. If it converted all of them now, its stake would come to about 23.8 per cent, so the 14.7 per cent figure is not a ceiling. Amazon put billions into Anthropic in 2023 and 2024, and the notes are the legacy of that funding.

The report also describes Anthropic's wider relationships with chip and cloud suppliers. TechCrunch also says major technology companies have agreed to buy a combined $26 billion of non-voting stock, with Google and Nvidia each committing $10 billion. Anthropic, for its part, has committed to spend more than $100 billion on cloud services over the next decade.

Why the numbers matter: a listing would make Anthropic's ownership public and open the company to the scrutiny that applies to listed firms. Large stakes held by suppliers that are also commercial partners will draw questions from investors about independence and about how much of the company's revenue flows back to the same backers.

stories.title: Google will keep Gemini chats for two months, up from 72 hours, even when history is off
stories.deck: The longer retention rolls out worldwide over the coming weeks; Google says it needs the time to respond to users and protect its services.
summary: Google is lengthening how long it holds on to conversations with its Gemini assistant, even for people who have switched chat history off. Under an update that TechCrunch says will roll out globally over the coming weeks, Gemini will retain chats for two months, up from the previous 72 hours.

Google's stated reason is operational. The company says it keeps chats for longer so it can respond to users, process feedback and protect its services and users. It did not answer TechCrunch's questions about what prompted the change, or whether it alters how conversations can be accessed or reviewed.

There is a counterweight in the settings. Google says two new controls will be off by default for people who had previously turned off its Keep Activity setting, and that people who had it on will see their chat history remain enabled. In other words, the longer retention applies in the background, while use of chats for improving models remains a separate choice. Gadgets 360 also reported on Wednesday that Gemini users can now save their chat history without opting in to AI model training.

For context, rivals hold temporary conversations for about a month. TechCrunch notes that OpenAI may keep temporary chats in ChatGPT for up to 30 days and that Anthropic retains incognito chats in Claude for 30 days by default. Gemini's new two-month window is therefore roughly double the period used by those two services.

stories.title: Nadella says he is now 'AGI-pilled', and warns that one dominant AI firm would be a disaster for everyone
stories.deck: Microsoft's chief executive also says he does not think frontier models such as Claude are conscious and backs Mustafa Suleyman's line on model rights.
summary: Microsoft chief executive Satya Nadella said at a roundtable after his Ignite keynote in San Francisco that he has become "AGI-pilled", but in a specific sense. He said he means it at the level of the economy: how the political economy might be organised around artificial general intelligence, and how politics might change because of it. He was speaking to The Verge's Nilay Patel.

Nadella drew a line at consciousness. Asked about frontier models such as Anthropic's Claude, he said he does not think they are conscious, adding that he is not dogmatic about the debate. He said he follows the view of Mustafa Suleyman, who leads Microsoft's AI division, that companies should not give models rights or treat them as having moral status. According to The Verge, Suleyman has criticised Anthropic's approach as dangerous, and Patel put that criticism to Nadella.

His main worry was concentration. If one firm ends up dominating, Nadella said, then "it's over, right? For all of us", a remark he framed with a reference to a Marxist view of a single firm owning everything. He said the priority should be broad diffusion of the technology, and he raised the risk of economic collapse and democratic failure if power gathers in one place.

The comments come as Microsoft markets its own AI products against Anthropic's, including an office suite release that prompted Patel's question. They are views offered in conversation, not announcements of policy, and Nadella did not describe any change to Microsoft's plans.

stories.title: Reliance explores a satellite network to rival Starlink, with completion pushed to 2035
stories.deck: People familiar with the plan say the group is talking to manufacturers about a roughly 1,600-satellite low-earth-orbit constellation.
summary: Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Group is exploring manufacturing partnerships for a broadband satellite constellation that would give India a home-controlled alternative to Elon Musk's Starlink, the Economic Times reports. The paper cites people familiar with the matter, so the plan is unconfirmed. The network would orbit close to Earth, serve Jio Platforms, and is described as roughly 1,600 satellites, with completion targeted for 2035.

The timeline has slipped. An earlier goal of 2030 was pushed back to 2035 because of constraints, the sources said. They described a staged approach: a test mission around September 2027 and deployment starting in early 2028. Reliance is said to be in talks with domestic manufacturers, startups and industrial groups, as well as two US firms and European suppliers. Chinese suppliers are excluded.

Manufacturing capacity is the bottleneck. India currently builds fewer than 15 satellites a year, while a constellation of this size would need about 200 annually, so the plan reportedly combines domestic production with at least 400 satellites imported from the United States. The sources said the system would serve connectivity and strategic communications, including during conflicts.

Launch capacity is the other worry. Amal Chandran, chief executive of the space start-up HEX20, told the paper that building satellites at scale is doable, but the real challenge is ensuring enough rocket launches happen in India to place them in the right orbit if Indian launch vehicles are used. Bharti Airtel's Sunil Mittal has separately argued that India must hold a satellite "kill switch" and avoid depending on a single provider.

stories.title: Tata Trusts row sharpens: Khambata answers Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh as RBI presses for a Tata Sons listing
stories.deck: The central bank has for the first time used the word 'listing' in its communication to Tata Sons, and Jimmy Tata has backed both the RBI and Chandrasekaran.
summary: The dispute inside the Tata Trusts, which control Tata Sons, escalated on Tuesday as trustee Darius Khambata hit back at fellow trustees Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh in a four-page letter, according to the Indian Express. He accused them of avoiding the real issues, presenting facts selectively and resorting to personal attacks, and questioned their sudden change of position on whether Tata Sons should be listed.

Khambata's central argument concerned consistency. He pointed out that the two had supported staying unlisted in March 2024, May 2025 and July 2025, before changing their stance in April 2026. He rejected the claim that he had undermined Srinivasan and said all trustees had agreed on 13 August to respect N Chandrasekaran's wish not to seek reappointment. The paper reports his account; the other two trustees have their own version, set out in an 11 November communication that questioned the seven-month uncertainty over Chandrasekaran's future.

Pressure from the regulator is mounting. The Indian Express reported on Monday that the Reserve Bank of India told Tata Sons to comply with all upper-layer NBFC rules, including the listing requirement, the first time the word has been used explicitly in its communication to the group. Governor Sanjay Malhotra has explained that core investment companies in the upper layer are required to list because of the systemic risk they pose. Noel Tata had maintained that earlier correspondence did not specifically mention listing.
The family dimension is also visible. Jimmy N Tata, the younger brother of the late Ratan Tata, has backed the RBI directive and Chandrasekaran's reappointment.

stories.title: Indian crew member missing after LPG tanker is attacked in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.deck: India condemns the attack on the Panama-flagged Tara Gas; 21 of the 24 Indians aboard are ashore in Oman.
summary: One Indian seafarer is missing and two are injured after the Panama-flagged liquefied petroleum gas tanker Tara Gas was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, according to India's Ministry of External Affairs. Twenty-four Indian nationals were on board. The ministry said 21 have been brought safely ashore at Khasab in Oman and the two injured crew members are in hospital. Search operations for the missing man are continuing, and his identity has not been made public.

India condemned the attack on Tuesday. The ministry called the continuing attacks on shipping deeply worrying, said the targeting of commercial vessels and civilian infrastructure must end, and called for freedom of navigation to be restored. It thanked the government of Oman for timely help with the rescue. The Indian embassy in Muscat is monitoring the search and relief effort.

Shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal said on X that the tanker was subjected to a subsequent attack that forced the entire crew to abandon the vessel, and that the government is coordinating with the ship's management company and regional rescue authorities. The Times of India's account matches the ministry's casualty figures. Reports differed on how many crew were aboard in total, with one account citing a 25-member crew, and the full circumstances of the attack have not been established.

The Times of India adds that the toll for Indian seafarers since the West Asia war began in February is rising: it cites government data showing 102 incidents in the region and 11 Indian lives lost, with the latest man bringing to four the number of Indian crew missing.

stories.title: Kulgam hunt for Lashkar commander continues as a fresh encounter breaks out
stories.deck: Security forces trace the movements of the men behind the 11 November attack on a CRPF checkpoint, while Kashmir's leaders criticise restrictions on residents.
summary: Security forces in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district are continuing a cordon-and-search operation for the people behind the 11 November attack on a CRPF checkpoint at Akhran, in which three personnel were injured. On Wednesday morning a fresh encounter broke out between militants and a joint team of the J&K Police and security forces, the Times of India reported, citing officials and a post by Kashmir Zone Police. Details of casualties were not immediately available.

The main target is Lateef Ahmad Bhat, a Lashkar-e-Taiba commander with a Rs 15 lakh bounty on his head. The Times of India says CCTV footage shows him and a local man, Umar Nisar Dar, visiting several villages on 10 November, the day before the attack, and that Dar had given Bhat shelter for five or six months. On Monday a suspected associate was shot dead in Laroo village. The Indian Express reports that the dead man is believed to be a 19-year-old, reported missing by his family a day earlier, and that sources identify him as Dar. His identity has not been officially confirmed.

The operation has drawn criticism of how it affects civilians. CPI(M) leader M Y Tarigami told the paper that restrictions on residents are "neither fair nor acceptable" and that ordinary people should not bear the brunt. National Conference MLA Imran Nabi Dar called the prolonged curbs avoidable, and Mehbooba Mufti alleged that Kulgam has been turned into a cantonment, warning of alienation and resentment. A senior police officer said the forces are cooperating with the public.
Bhat's whereabouts are still unknown, and the search is continuing through the area.

stories.title: Quad leaders meet in Manila, unveil maritime, business and AI plans as Trump says his 'phone and office are open'
stories.deck: The first Quad summit in two years announces a maritime-patrol exercise in March 2027 and a business forum in Mumbai; Modi also pitches a seafarer-security initiative at the East Asia Summit.
summary: The leaders of the Quad grouping met in Manila on Tuesday, on the sidelines of the East Asia Summit, for their first summit in two years. US President Donald Trump, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Australia's Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced a series of initiatives, according to the Indian Express and the Times of India.

The plans include the Quad's first military exercise involving maritime patrol aircraft, P-8s and P-3Cs, in Guam in March 2027, under an Indo-Pacific maritime surveillance partnership launched in May. A first Quad Business Leaders' Forum will be held in Mumbai in early 2027, announced by foreign ministry spokesman Randhir Jaiswal, and Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri said the leaders agreed to launch it. Leaders also backed an AI accelerator, with the Indian Express reporting that more than $85 million is being spent to widen access to trusted AI ecosystems.

Trump called the grouping "very important and special", said his phone and Oval Office are always open to India, Japan and Australia, and described Modi as a friend and great leader. The Times of India says he framed the exercise as protecting "peace through strength" and spoke of critical-mineral deals among members. Modi described the Quad as a "trusted partnership" offering trusted solutions for the Indo-Pacific.

Doubts hung over the meeting. The Times of India notes that the question was not whether the Quad would survive but at what level it would operate, and that the joint release did not acknowledge a date for the next summit. Modi pitched a meeting in early 2027. Separately, the Times of India reports that at the East Asia Summit Modi announced an international initiative to secure the safety of seafarers.
This follows Tuesday's earlier coverage of the leaders' arrival, and adds the outcomes of the talks.

stories.title: Agnipath revamp: talks focus on how many Agniveers become regular soldiers, and on what skills count
stories.deck: Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff says selection criteria for the 75 per cent offered a two-year extension are still 'under deliberation'.
summary: As the government reworks the Agnipath short-service recruitment scheme, the armed forces are still deciding how to choose which soldiers will stay on, the Indian Express reports. Under the revised approach, 75 per cent of Agniveers would be offered a two-year extension, taking service to six years, while 25 per cent would be selected on merit for regular service after four years. Responding to the paper's queries about eligibility, Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff said the selection criteria are "presently under deliberation".

The paper describes ideas on the table without presenting any as settled. They include objective criteria that would exclude those placed in a low medical category or with alcohol dependency, with dispensation for battle casualties and medical problems attributable to military service. Another idea is retention rules that allow for minor disciplinary infringements, and a cadre test at unit level. Multi-skilling and technology proficiency are among the attributes under discussion for the longer-serving group. All of this is described as evolving or preliminary.

An official told the paper that criteria are set after monitoring troops over many years, adding that there have been a substantial number of low-medical-category cases among regular soldiers in recent years, mainly because of lifestyle diseases. That experience appears to be driving the interest in health and fitness benchmarks.
The report comes days after more than 2,700 Agniveers, including 142 women, completed training at INS Chilka in Odisha.

stories.title: Ukraine cuts the Crimean Bridge's road span in an overnight missile and drone attack
stories.deck: Zelensky calls it an 'unprecedented operation'; the Kremlin says the bridge will be rebuilt 'better than before'. The rail span was also hit, but some trains have reportedly resumed.
summary: Ukraine has badly damaged the Crimean Bridge, the symbol of Russia's hold on the annexed peninsula, in an overnight attack with cruise missiles and drones, the BBC reports. A large arched section of the road bridge fell into the water, and Ukraine's military says the roadway is out of action with no vehicles able to cross. The parallel rail section was hit by drones, but its supporting arch stayed standing and some rail services later resumed.

President Volodymyr Zelensky called it an "unprecedented operation", weeks in the making, carried out in seven stages with several types of drone and with Flamingo and Neptune cruise missiles. Ukraine's security service said operations over a month had systematically suppressed Russian air defences. Russia's Investigative Committee confirmed structural damage and opened a terrorism case. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would be rebuilt "better than before", and did not rule out a link between the strikes and President Vladimir Putin's visit to China.

The bridge cost about $3.6 billion, was built after the 2014 annexation, and was opened by Putin in May 2018. Russia said it had shot down 2,256 drones, which would make this the biggest Ukrainian drone attack of the war. The BBC says the long-term effect of the strike is not yet clear.

In Kyiv, Russian ballistic missiles targeted the Pivdennyi (Southern) and Pivnichnyi (Northern) bridges: Zelensky said four missiles were aimed at the first and three at the second. Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said traffic had partly resumed and that critical infrastructure, heating and water supplies were damaged. A Kyiv resident told the BBC the Crimea attack would be "a very heavy blow to the morale of the Russians".
The claims about the attack's planning and aims come from the Ukrainian and Russian governments. This updates yesterday's edition, which reported the first drone hit on the bridge.

stories.title: United States loses measles elimination status after 26 years
stories.deck: The Pan American Health Organization says the same strain circulated for more than 12 months; the US has recorded more than 5,400 cases and 10 deaths this year.
summary: The United States has lost the measles elimination status it held for 26 years, after the Pan American Health Organization concluded that the same strain of the virus had spread without interruption for more than 12 months. The BBC reports that Mexico and Bolivia also lost their status in the same ruling. Canada lost its own last year.

The US has recorded more than 5,400 measles cases this year, with 10 deaths, the highest toll since the early 1990s. A Pennsylvania outbreak has infected more than 1,400 people, probably an undercount, and killed seven. Vaccination coverage has fallen to 92.4 per cent, below the 95 per cent usually needed to stop spread. Two doses of the MMR vaccine are about 97 per cent effective. The BBC adds that the UK, Spain, Austria, Russia, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan lost the status earlier this year.

PAHO director Dr Jarbas Barbosa called the figures "a serious warning for our region". PAHO's Daniel Salas said countries that lost status must submit corrective action plans. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said it is committed to regaining it. Erica Schwartz of the CDC said it was vaccination, not the designation, that protects people, and that $100 million had gone to state and local health departments.

Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr said he continues to recommend MMR vaccination and argued that the rise began before he took office. Critics point to his firing last year of vaccine advisers, whose recommended changes were blocked by a federal judge. Dr Nuwan Gunawardhana called the loss "a huge leap backwards" and said confusing messages from the top are confusing families. The BBC says the CDC is for now declining to record some Pennsylvania deaths while Kennedy and state officials dispute how they should be counted.

stories.title: Russian military transport plane crashes in Siberia, killing all 19 on board
stories.deck: The defence ministry says a technical malfunction is the preliminary cause; an investigation is under way.
summary: A Russian military transport aircraft, an An-12, crashed in Siberia on Tuesday, killing all 19 people on board, according to the BBC, which cites Russian state media quoting the defence ministry. The aircraft went down during what the ministry called a scheduled flight, in an uninhabited area of the Kemerovo region near the village of Yagunovo.

The defence ministry said a technical malfunction is preliminarily believed to be the cause. That is an initial assessment from the operator, not a conclusion, and Russian aviation authorities have opened an investigation. The BBC's report does not give the names of the dead or say who was on board, beyond the total of 19.

The regional governor, Ilya Seredyuk, said an emergency response team had quickly put out a fire that broke out after the crash and that police sealed off the area. The report mentions no casualties on the ground.

The An-12 is a four-engined turboprop freighter first built in the Soviet Union in the 1950s, and versions remain in service with Russian forces and with civilian cargo operators. Its age is often raised after accidents, but nothing in the ministry's statement says whether that played a part here.

Kemerovo, in south-central Siberia, lies far from the front lines in Ukraine, and officials have not suggested hostile action. The account rests on the initial official statements, and further detail on the flight's purpose and passengers may emerge as the inquiry proceeds.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi tells Columbia audience India is 'sitting on an economic disaster'
stories.deck: The Congress leader cites unemployment and the education system; the claims are his own, and the report quotes no government response.
summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said on Wednesday that India is heading towards an economic crisis, pointing to what he called massive unemployment and a deep problem with the education system. He was speaking at an event at Columbia University in New York, during a two-day visit to the United States, the Times of India reports. His remarks are political opinion and have not been tested against data in the report.

Gandhi said India is "sitting on an economic disaster". He described young, formally educated middle-class Indians as people who no longer see a future for themselves and who are questioning the advice their parents gave them about studying and working hard. The question that prompted the answer, about India's youth, came from the moderator, Lydia Polgreen.

The Times of India says the visit also includes a stop at the University of Chicago. It does not quote any government response to Gandhi's comments, and it does not set out the official employment figures his statement would be measured against.

Because the report rests on a single outlet and on a speech, it should be read as a statement of the opposition's argument, not as an independent finding on the state of the economy. Readers who want to weigh the claim would look to the government's labour-force surveys and to growth data, including the Indian Express's report this week that GDP growth for July to September is expected to be near 8 per cent.

stories.title: Alonso and Loeb to drive for Aston Martin's factory team at the 2027 Dakar Rally
stories.deck: The Formula One driver, now 45, will race alongside Sebastien Loeb and Lucas Moraes in a Prodrive-built Dreadnought.
summary: Fernando Alonso will race in the Dakar Rally in January with Aston Martin, confirming months of speculation. Autosport reports that the Formula One driver will be part of a factory entry, Aston Martin's first in the event, run by Prodrive and badged as the Dreadnought. He will be joined by Sebastien Loeb and by Lucas Moraes, who won the 2025 World Rally-Raid Championship.

The 49th Dakar will take place in Portugal and Morocco from 9 to 23 January 2027, having been relocated from its original venue. Alonso, 45, made his Dakar debut in 2020 and finished 13th overall, with a second place on stage eight. His navigator will be Marc Coma. Loeb is contesting his 11th Dakar.

Alonso said he had to decide whether to take on both F1 and Dakar in the same year, that he respects the race, and that Formula One remains his priority. Aston Martin chief executive Adrian Hallmark described the Dreadnought's mission as dominating extreme terrain and called the line-up three great champions. Loeb spoke of his motivation to win the event and of taking on the challenge with Aston Martin.
Alonso's Dakar commitment sits alongside his Formula One work, and the rally comes after the F1 season ends. Nasser Al-Attiyah's plans for next season were not confirmed in the report.
For Aston Martin, the rally programme is a second showcase for the brand, alongside its Formula One entry.

stories.title: Tiger Woods set to return in December at the Hero World Challenge after two years away
stories.deck: The 50-year-old, who has not played a ranking event since the 2024 Open, says he is feeling better and has been training.
summary: Tiger Woods is set to return to competitive golf in December, his first tournament appearance in more than two years, BBC Sport reports. The 50-year-old, who has won 15 major titles, will play in the Hero World Challenge in the Bahamas, an event he hosts. He is in the 20-player field as one of three tournament exemptions, alongside Rickie Fowler and Gary Woodland. The event is part of the PGA Tour schedule but offers no FedEx Cup points.

Woods has not played a traditional ranking event since the 2024 Open Championship at Royal Troon. His comeback follows a difficult stretch. He has had multiple back surgeries, serious leg fractures from a 2021 car crash and a ruptured Achilles tendon in 2025, and his mother died in February 2025. In April he was arrested in Florida and charged with driving under the influence after a crash, and in September he accepted a five-year driving ban under a plea agreement in a reckless-driving case. His attorney said he had stepped away to take part in an "intensive, highly individualised and medically integrated" treatment programme.

Woods himself struck an upbeat note: "I'm feeling better, no doubt about that. I've been training quite a bit. I will be at Hero either way, so I'll see you there." The last sentence leaves open how much he will play, since he attends as host in any case.
His partner, Vanessa Trump, was diagnosed with breast cancer earlier this year and said last month she is cancer-free, according to the BBC.

stories.title: Bryson DeChambeau joins the DP World Tour after the collapse of LIV Golf
stories.deck: The two-time US Open champion applied before the deadline and will play the Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa in December.
summary: Two-time US Open champion Bryson DeChambeau has agreed to join the DP World Tour for next season, in the clearest sign yet of how far the breakaway LIV Golf circuit has fallen, according to BBC Sport. DeChambeau, who left for LIV in 2022, submitted his application to join the European-based tour before Sunday's deadline. He has confirmed that he will play Gary Player's Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa in December.

LIV's future was put in doubt in April when Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its financial backing, and the tour has since confirmed that it intends to wind down its operations. Other big names have also announced they will leave, among them two-time major winner Jon Rahm and England's Lee Westwood.

DeChambeau said he "gave everything" to try to keep LIV Golf alive. In May he had denied reports that he was looking to leave before the end of the year, so the move marks a reversal of what he said at the time.

The details of how LIV's members will fit into the professional game remain unsettled. BBC Sport's report does not say what status DeChambeau will have on other tours, or how his DP World Tour schedule will be built.
For the DP World Tour, signing a player of DeChambeau's profile adds star power at a time when the sport's landscape has been shifting since the breakaway began.

stories.title: Over 30 villages in Gujarat's Valsad district say poor mobile coverage is endangering residents
stories.deck: A memorandum from Kaprada and Nanaponda areas demands towers; the district collector says BSNL has been urged to build them.
summary: More than 30 villages in Valsad district, in South Gujarat, say poor or absent mobile coverage is putting residents at risk, according to the Indian Express. A memorandum submitted to the authorities on Tuesday by people in Kaprada taluka and the Nanaponda area says the situation has become dire and could have serious, even life-threatening, consequences for the local population. Around 500 families in one settlement alone are affected.

The villages named include Kakad, Kopar Kajali, Varana, Ozar, Sukhala, Mani, Chijda, Piparoni, Meghval, Rohyal, Talat, Vadi, Chandvegan and Dinbari. The paper says the problem has been raised before. Kaprada BJP MLA Jitubhai Chaudhary asked for mobile towers on 16 July, and Dakshaben Gaikwad, a district panchayat member, wrote to the district collector on 3 September.

Jayendra Gavit, a non-political tribal leader, said it is time to move beyond proposals and assurances. He said the community is ready to launch an agitation demanding a BSNL or other government telecom tower to serve 13 surrounding settlements, and will protest more strongly if no concrete action follows.

Valsad Collector Nitin Sangwan acknowledged the problem. He said there are network problems in some interior areas, that government pockets have been identified, and that BSNL has been urged to set up towers. He said work would start and that the issue would be resolved "in the coming days". No dates or number of towers were given in the report.
